Fish’s double-time gallop fuels this rock-opera behemoth while Trey slashes power chords and soars into an arena-rock solo. Page goes full Steinman with dramatic piano flourishes, and Mike locks in like a runaway train. As the final ascent peaks, Trey wails, the crowd screams, and for a moment, this one might never land. It lands. As soon as it closes the show, I head on lot where I down my ritual post-show meal. I may be slamming a veggie burrito but my mind is on meatloaf.

This has to be AL. What a find, had no idea Burroughs made music. Super unique voice fits perfectly with these absurd “lyrics.” That voice is haunting. Spare. Ass. Annie. Really sticking with me, randomly popping into my head 😂

Even more points second time around. So much of this list felt very similar to me and this is way out there 

Ok I’m gonna put this comment here with my favorite pick of the week. Who am I to judge these voices? They were all great. I could give a point to every song. But I decided it had to come down to this: the song had to differentiate itself enough on this list, have a catchy melody or super unique vocal quality, while also having the voice be the most driving/defining force AND be a song I actually liked. You all deserved points for this round but I had to draw a line somewhere

longest.text: This one made me cry. For those of you who don't know, my (ex) father in law, who I loved a lot, was a folk singer and his singing partner was Josh White Jr, son of blues legend josh white who wrote timber (Jerry). Josh white jr (Donnie) plays just like his dad, no one else plays quite like it. His voice is beautiful. And that voice and the lyrics speared my heart like a perfect folk song ought to. He recently died. RIP to a master and his dad. No one will play guitar quite like they did again.

One of her best known songs as well as the most controversial record of her career. It's about the freedom a woman receives from birth control pills. The song tells a story of a wife who is upset about her husband getting her pregnant year after year, but is now happy bc she can control her own reproductive choices because she has "the pill" (which had been introduced in 1960). The song, like many of Lynn's other hits, suggested her personal life: she'd had SIX children, FOUR of whom were born BEFORE SHE WAS 20! The song's frank discussion of birth control, something that was considered risqué subject matter at the time (especially in country music), led to a number of country radio stations refusing to play it. In an interview, Lynn recounted how she had been congratulated after the song's success by a number of rural physicians, telling her how "The Pill" had done more to highlight the availability of birth control in isolated, rural areas, than all the literature they had released.

longest.text: I balance a wooden spoon on a cutting board to remind me that time is a wheel/Later, in my next life, I’ll come to this spoon, notice its unnatural posture, and realize my circuitry/A marinara-stained spoon as my key to the universe. Remember the spoon! You’ll need it/to see where you’ve come from, where you’re going. Don’t touch the spoon! Leave it on its axis, unnoticed/I like to throw corks into decanters while my sauce thickens. I set my basket by the sink and shoot hollow thuds into stained glass/tip the cork into the garbage then another game to play. My sauce throws garlic fumes into the fan/I lower the stove and find a cork-Boiron et Fils-and near it a spoon/A cork knuckles in the air when tossed-two quick strikes. On the third, my bat whips around and sends the cork soaring into the window/A victory lap as I go to retrieve it, bat in hand, soft, grainy. I look down/My Spoon! And think if I can't even preserve my bookmark to the next life, what a waste of space we truly are.
This round was the perfect opportunity to not pick an instrumental funk song. But it still slaps. The song doesn’t reference protein but I’ll allow it on account of the album and band name.

In 1995, I made the golf team.  I learned how to golf from my grandpa Charlie when I was 5, and he was the best person to golf with ever.  Our golf coach was a single man who drove a conversion van that fit 15 people.  He no joke was a recovered alcholic and replaced booze with Coca-Cola. He literally drank over a 6 pack every day and the cans would be in his trunk.  He also used to scream at you and call you a "commie" if you took too long lining up a putt. 

My senior year I won ideal teammate

Although Parsons had said he wanted his body cremated at Joshua Tree and his ashes spread over the formation Cap Rock, Parsons' stepfather organized a private ceremony in New Orleans and left the body in the care of a funeral home. To fulfill Parsons' wishes, Kaufman and a friend stole both a hearse and his body and drove it to Joshua Tree. At Cap Rock Parking Lot, they poured gasoline into the open coffin and lit it, creating an enormous fireball. They were arrested and fined $750.00.
